source.title: Not All Knowledge Is Created Equal
source.authors: Zi-Yun Li; Xinshao Wang; Hao-Jin Yang; Diane Hu; N. Robertson; D. Clifton; C. Meinel

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Tests performance under synthetic label noise and reports clean-test accuracy, but does not measure training error or use completely random labels.
record.gate_note: The study reports test accuracy under 20%–80% synthetic noise, not training error on random labels. It does not report fitting time, unstructured inputs, regularization removal, or learning order.
record.test_reason: The study uses noisy-label memorization as motivation for a mitigation method and reports clean-test accuracy. It does not measure fitting corrupted training labels, memorization rates, or learning order. Its method comparisons therefore do not test V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that selecting confident knowledge improves mutual distillation, outperforming compared MKD methods under label noise while remaining competitive in clean settings. They do not establish fitting completely random labels.
record.recipe_differences: Trains models with synthetic or real-world noisy labels and mutual distillation or label-correction methods; does not train on fully random labels to measure memorization.
record.method_sensitivity: Test accuracy varies with synthetic noise rate, noise type, and training method.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 2 reports ResNet34 cross-entropy clean-test accuracy of 75.58% with clean labels, 63.31% with 20% symmetric noise, and 47.20% with 40% symmetric noise. No corresponding training accuracy is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Partial synthetic label corruption reduces clean-test accuracy in the tested standard-training setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 1 reports that selective mutual distillation improves clean-test accuracy over zero or all knowledge transfer across the four tested self-training methods at 40% symmetric noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Selecting confident knowledge for mutual distillation improves robustness to label noise in the tested configurations.

record.code_released: The code will be released once this work is accepted.
record.peer_reviewed: 2022 Trustworthy and Socially Responsible Machine Learning (TSRML 2022), co-located with NeurIPS 2022.
record.problems: No training-error results on noisy or random labels are reported. The relevant synthetic-noise results report final test accuracy only, and the highest tested noise rate is 80%.
record.rows_left_out: No rows extracted: the reported test accuracies under partial label noise do not establish whether the networks fit the corrupted training labels, as V4 requires.

untested.parts: Fitting completely random labels to zero or near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Relative time to fit true versus random labels and convergence slowdown with increasing corruption.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect training-set fitting across corruption levels and its joint progression with test error toward chance. Clean-test accuracies under partial corruption are reported, but training fitting is not measured and corruption stops at 80%.
Whether explicit regularization prevents fitting random labels and whether removing it harms generalization on true labels.
Whether shared real-data patterns are learned before noisy labels. Progressive distillation thresholds do not measure this learning order.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T2 classification and V4 tested_not_extracted designation should be corrected. Leaving the result rows empty is appropriate; the reported robustness comparisons do not establish the training-set memorization required by the claim versions.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labels, zero or near-zero training error, test error at chance, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Training time and convergence slowdown as label corruption increases.
Shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
The paper reports test accuracy as synthetic noise rates increase, but does not report training error; its noise rates stop at 80%, not all labels corrupted.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevent fitting random labels, and whether removing them affects true-label generalization.
Whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
